title: secp256k1-ecdlp: truncated-coverage deterministic BSGS with a rebalanced table

claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r), input Q=[x]P for the fixed standard secp256k1 generator P, the deterministic truncated-coverage baby-step/giant-step algorithm in proof.md recovers x exactly whenever x < H*m, which is a fraction H*m/r >= 2/5 of the uniform challenge space, using at most 2^128.339838 total target-group-operation equivalents, including preprocessing and verification. Peak memory is at most 2^135.338662 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^127.339838 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in total work; nonuniform advice is at most 2^0 bytes and is included in memory. Inputs outside [0,H*m) exhaust the fixed giant loop and return no output; that failure path is charged at the same worst-case bound, and there is no randomness, retry, restart or amplification. This is a classical cold attack with no uncharged advice, quantum steps or heuristic assumptions. The exponential memory is required. This is an analytic generic accounting control, not a claim of novelty or practical execution.

experiments.purpose: Exhaustively check the truncated-coverage baby-step/giant-step rule on a small additive cyclic group: every covered scalar is recovered, every uncovered scalar exhausts the fixed loop, and the coverage fraction is at least 2/5. This does not establish production curve behavior, memory bounds, or operation costs.
